stem.text: The temperature at a point x meters from one end of a metal rod is T(x) degrees Celsius. Suppose that \( T'(1) = 2 \). Write this statement in Leibniz notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( \left. \frac{dT}{dx} \right|_{x=1} = 2 \), so the rate of change of the temperature with respect to the distance along the rod when x = 1 is 2 degrees Celsius per meter.

worked_solution.text: In \( T'(1) \) the function is T, the independent variable is x, and the derivative is evaluated at x = 1, so the statement is about one input only.
In Leibniz notation the same statement is \( \left. \frac{dT}{dx} \right|_{x=1} = 2 \).
It says that the rate of change of the temperature with respect to the distance along the rod when x = 1 is 2 degrees Celsius per meter.

options.label: \( \frac{dT}{dx} = 2 \), so the rate of change of the temperature with respect to the distance along the rod, the same at every x, is 2 degrees Celsius per meter.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the derivative function

options.label: \( \frac{T(1)}{1} = 2 \), so the temperature divided by the distance along the rod when x = 1 is 2 degrees Celsius per meter.
options.derivation: the Leibniz fraction read as the quotient of the two quantities at the point

options.label: \( \left. \frac{dT}{dx} \right|_{x=1} = 2 \), so the rate of change of the temperature with respect to the distance along the rod when x = 1 is 2 degrees Celsius per meter.
\( \left. \frac{dx}{dT} \right|_{x=1} = 2 \), so the rate of change of the distance along the rod with respect to the temperature when x = 1 is 2 meters per degree Celsius.
options.derivation: the roles of the two variables exchanged, so the derivative is read with respect to the dependent variable
